**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:11005)

**Proposed mechanism:** SLC2A1 (HGNC:11005) —DISRUPTS→ Glucose transport into brain and erythrocytes (REACT:R-HSA-70189); Glucose transport into brain and erythrocytes (REACT:R-HSA-70189) —DECREASES→ Glucose (CHEBI:17234); Glucose (CHEBI:17234) —LEADS_TO→ Seizures (HP:0001250); Glucose (CHEBI:17234) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263); Glucose (CHEBI:17234) —LEADS_TO→ Microcephaly (HP:0000252); Glucose (CHEBI:17234) —LEADS_TO→ Failure to thrive (HP:0011961); Glucose (CHEBI:17234) —LEADS_TO→ Ataxia (HP:0001251); Glucose (CHEBI:17234) —LEADS_TO→ Progressive neurological decline (HP:0002363); Glucose (CHEBI:17234) —LEADS_TO→ Hypoglycorrhachia (HP:0003476). Pathogenic variants in SLC2A1 impair glucose transport into the brain and erythrocytes, leading to glucose deficiency in these tissues. This cellular energy deficit manifests as a spectrum of neurological and developmental phenotypes common to both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of individuals with pathogenic SLC2A1 variants who do not present with any of the shared core phenotypes, or identification of a distinct molecular mechanism for one of the diseases that does not involve SLC2A1 dysfunction. _(variant: Presence of common benign variants in SLC2A1 (e.g., allele frequency > 1% in gnomAD) that are fully penetrant for either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared molecular basis in SLC2A1 allows for the investigation of common therapeutic strategies, such as ketogenic diets or direct glucose supplementation, which aim to bypass the defective transporter and provide alternative energy sources to the brain.
